sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 5: Classical and Quantum Circuits (updated July 2015)
sources.locator: Complete 54-page Chapter 5 PDF, read in full in the existing QC source record; this author inspected §5.2.2, printed pp.14–19, and §5.2.3, printed pp.20–22. Relevant arguments are summarized per item; citations do not replace local proofs.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas
contents.reason: Preskill supplies the compute-copy-reverse setting; the exact operator-level clean/dirty contracts are stated locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: lem-qc-ancilla-identities-stable-under-reference-and-mixtures
contents.reason: The source does not prove the arbitrary-reference and mixed-matrix extensions; the local matrix-unit and tensor-identity proof supplies them.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: def-qc-toffoli-and-fredkin
contents.reason: Preskill defines Toffoli and CNOT; Fredkin is additionally defined locally and is not attributed to the source.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: lem-qc-x-cnot-toffoli-and-fredkin-are-involutions
contents.reason: The Toffoli/CNOT conventions are corroborated; the Fredkin involution and decomposition are verified locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: lem-qc-toffoli-clean-target-and-uncomputation
contents.reason: The source describes Toffoli evaluation and compute-copy-reverse; the exact four-case target identity is proved locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: alg-qc-reversible-embedding
contents.reason: The source gives reversible Boolean simulation context; the finite gate-list procedure, invalid-input branch, and exact port handling are specified locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: lem-qc-fresh-target-not-and-or-gadgets
contents.reason: The source supplies the NOT/CNOT/Toffoli gates; the particular fresh-target OR formula and truth table are proved locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: def-qc-coherent-function-oracle
contents.reason: Equation (5.27) defines the one-bit XOR embedding; the definition extends it to total multi-output functions and an explicit query contract.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-reversible-embedding-cost
contents.reason: The source motivates compute-copy-reverse and notes its gate overhead; the exact $6S+4E+m$ gate bound and workspace count are proved locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary
contents.reason: Equation (5.27) exhibits the self-inverse one-bit map; the arbitrary multi-output, noninjective case is proved locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-phase-kickback-from-xor-oracle
contents.reason: Chapter 5 does not supply the phase-kickback argument; the complete character-target calculation is proved locally.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-reversible-embedding-parallel-depth
contents.reason: The source does not give the same-layer fanout-tree schedule or stated logarithmic depth bound; the local proof supplies both.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-clean-uncomputation-restores-workspace
contents.reason: The source describes copying the output and reversing the full computation; the local theorem gives the exact register action and hypotheses.

contents.name: Preskill Chapter 5: thm-qc-oracle-phase-query-cost-boundary
contents.reason: Chapter 5 does not provide the query-versus-gate boundary; the result is treated by de Wolf and proved from the local access contract.

sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: Complete 239-page lecture-notes PDF, read in full in the existing QC source record; this author inspected §§2.1.2–2.4, printed pp.14–17. Relevant arguments are summarized per item; citations do not replace local proofs.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas
contents.reason: Workspace initialized to zero and reversible evaluation are discussed; the exact clean/dirty contracts are made explicit locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: lem-qc-ancilla-identities-stable-under-reference-and-mixtures
contents.reason: The notes do not prove this operator-level extension; the batch proves it directly.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: def-qc-toffoli-and-fredkin
contents.reason: The notes define CNOT and Toffoli; Fredkin is added locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: lem-qc-x-cnot-toffoli-and-fredkin-are-involutions
contents.reason: The Toffoli action is corroborated; the Fredkin checks and circuit decomposition are local.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: lem-qc-toffoli-clean-target-and-uncomputation
contents.reason: Toffoli-based reversible computation is described and extended to quantum superpositions; the clean-target identity is verified locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: alg-qc-reversible-embedding
contents.reason: Section 2.3 explains compiling a classical function by Toffoli gates; this item supplies the exact finite instructions and input validation locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: lem-qc-fresh-target-not-and-or-gadgets
contents.reason: The elementary gates are present; the particular NOT and OR gadgets are verified locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: def-qc-coherent-function-oracle
contents.reason: Section 2.4 defines the XOR oracle on address and target bits and separates query access from ordinary circuits.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-reversible-embedding-cost
contents.reason: The notes support reversible simulation, but not the precise port-sensitive gate/work bound, which is derived locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary
contents.reason: Section 2.4 states the XOR query as a permutation and hence unitary; the general total multi-output case is proved locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-phase-kickback-from-xor-oracle
contents.reason: Section 2.4 derives the phase query using the $| - angle$ target; the multi-output character version is proved locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-reversible-embedding-parallel-depth
contents.reason: The notes do not establish the exact private-fanout-tree depth bound; it is proved locally.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-clean-uncomputation-restores-workspace
contents.reason: Section 2.3 describes coherent function computation; the local item supplies the exact copy-and-inverse identity.

contents.name: de Wolf §§2.1.2–2.4: thm-qc-oracle-phase-query-cost-boundary
contents.reason: Section 2.4 distinguishes black-box query input from standard circuit cost and derives phase access; the controlled/inverse caveats are proved from local contracts.
